title: How GTA 6 Makes Its Money Back

shots.name: HOOK
shots.narration: Rockstar has spent an estimated $1.5 billion building GTA 6. It's been 13 years since the last one. And it comes out in {days} days. So how do they make that money back?
shots.visual: Dark empty ground. The counter slams in, red: -$1,500,000,000. City blocks pop up one by one. A calendar tile flips to '{days} DAYS'.
shots.tts_text: Rockstar has spent an estimated one and a half billion dollars building GTA 6. It's been thirteen years since the last one. And it comes out in {days_words} days. So how do they make that money back?

shots.name: THE PRICE
shots.narration: Start with the price. $80 a copy. But the store that sells it keeps a cut, around 30 percent. So Rockstar's side sees about $56.
shots.visual: A giant game case lands in the plaza with an '$80' tag. A slice of the coin stack slides into a storefront. The rest reads '$56'.
shots.tts_text: Start with the price. Eighty dollars a copy. But the store that sells it keeps a cut, around thirty percent. So Rockstar's side sees about fifty-six dollars.

shots.name: THE TARGET
shots.narration: Which means they need to sell about 27 million copies just to get back to zero.
shots.visual: Tiny buyers queue through the streets, snaking around every block. '27 MILLION' pops in. The counter barely moves.
shots.tts_text: Which means they need to sell about twenty-seven million copies just to get back to zero.

shots.name: THE BASELINE
shots.narration: Is that a lot? The last game, GTA 5, made $1 billion in its first three days. It has sold 235 million copies. And it's still selling.
shots.visual: An older district marked '2013'. One tower shoots up to '$1B' in three quick beats, then keeps growing. '235M' pops in.
shots.tts_text: Is that a lot? The last game, GTA 5, made one billion dollars in its first three days. It has sold two hundred and thirty-five million copies. And it's still selling.

shots.name: THE HEAD START
shots.narration: And GTA 6 has a head start. One estimate puts pre-orders above 10 million copies. That's about $1 billion in sales before anyone has played it. The company's own CEO calls it unprecedented.
shots.visual: Night, shops closed. Armoured trucks arrive anyway and unload into the vault. The red counter climbs to about -$800,000,000.
shots.tts_text: And GTA 6 has a head start. One estimate puts pre-orders above ten million copies. That's about one billion dollars in sales before anyone has played it. The company's own CEO calls it unprecedented.

shots.name: THE LAUNCH
shots.narration: Then comes launch. One analyst expects 38 million copies in the first year. Another expects over $3 billion in sales. Either way, the red number turns green.
shots.visual: Sunrise. Every shop opens at once and coins stream to the vault from all districts. The counter races through zero and flips green. The city lights up.
shots.tts_text: Then comes launch. One analyst expects thirty-eight million copies in the first year. Another expects over three billion dollars in sales. Either way, the red number turns green.

shots.name: THE LONG TAIL
shots.narration: And that's only the game. The online mode is projected to add around $500 million a year, for as long as people keep playing.
shots.visual: Apartment windows blink on across the city, each dropping a small coin toward the vault in a stream that never stops.
shots.tts_text: And that's only the game. The online mode is projected to add around five hundred million dollars a year, for as long as people keep playing.

shots.name: THE ENDING
shots.narration: The biggest estimate puts the lifetime total at $10 billion. Those are projections. The real number starts counting in {days} days.
shots.visual: Pull back to the whole glowing city. The counter shows '$10B?'. The calendar tile flips from {days} to {days_next}. Cut to black.
shots.tts_text: The biggest estimate puts the lifetime total at ten billion dollars. Those are projections. The real number starts counting in {days_words} days.
